packs.title: Shape and Shore
packs.promise: Read distinctive buildings, canal crossings and the Marina shoreline across Dubai.

q.s: Find three exterior details in a dhow-inspired building.
st: Find a curved roof edge, a glass wall and a patterned exterior screen, or locate them in the Opera’s video.
Read the venue’s account of the dhow inspiration. Choose which of your three details most suggests a boat to you and mark that choice as your interpretation.
Save the three details and your interpretation in a sketch or short note. Observe the building without tracing or copying its logos.

q.s: Plan a short canal segment beside a forked bridge.
st: Locate the suspension bridge near Sheikh Zayed Road on the map and choose a short open promenade segment with a clear turn-back point. You can plan without walking.
Trace your plan, or walk only that short segment when conditions suit you. Find a forked support and a cable line in the view or contractor photograph.
Save the segment, turn-back choice and two structural lines. Finish on land and keep shared paths and bridge approaches clear.

q.s: Pause with a built silhouette and the open sea.
st: Choose a comfortable stopped place on the open promenade, or use the source photograph. Find a built silhouette toward Bluewaters and a stretch of open horizon.
Pause for about a minute and compare the bounded shape with the open horizontal line. Shorten the pause or move when conditions do not suit you.
Save one word for each shape and choose whether to finish your outing here. Keep beach entrances and shared walking space clear.

packs.title: Creek and Courtyards
packs.promise: Find a smaller Dubai in the textures and turns beside the Creek.

q.s: Find three shapes that leave nothing behind.
st: Choose an open public lane in Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, keeping doors and narrow passages clear.
Find a patch of shade with a straight edge, a curved edge and an interrupted edge. If light is flat, use three shapes in the built surfaces.
Describe the three shapes and choose the one that would make a useful symbol for this part of your day.

q.s: Make a palette from one comfortable viewpoint.
st: Choose a comfortable public place on the Al Seef promenade with a view of water and building surfaces.
Collect three color impressions: one from water, one from a wall and one from shadow. If color perception differs, use lightness and texture instead.
Give each an original two-word name, then decide how much of a small imaginary color card each would occupy.

q.s: Turn a waterfront view into three original moments.
st: Choose a clear promenade position and look along the Creek without following a particular person or boat.
Pick three non-human details: something still, something moving and something partly hidden.
Write a three-sentence imagined scene using those details.
